subject: Oceanography
title: The Southern Oscillation
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Southern Oscillation.

hook.text: In 1924, Gilbert Walker found that air pressure in Tahiti and Darwin seesaws—when one rises, the other falls.

buildup.text: This atmospheric seesaw is the Southern Oscillation—the pressure pattern that pairs with El Niño.

discovery.text: Together they form ENSO—the most powerful natural climate cycle, affecting billions of people.

twist.text: Jacob Bjerknes connected the ocean and atmosphere pieces in the 1960s—showing they're one coupled system.

climax.text: ENSO prediction is now possible months ahead—giving farmers and governments time to prepare.

punchline.text: A pressure seesaw between two islands drives weather for the whole world.

quiz.question: What is ENSO?
options: The coupled ocean-atmosphere cycle of El Niño and Southern Oscillation
